name: Judas
overview: Judas was a male member of the tribe of Judah and is identified as a "brother" of Jesus, being born of the same womb to Mary. This relationship indicates a close familial connection within the immediate household of Jesus, highlighting his place in the family lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Judas, meaning "praised," is a proper name found in the New Testament and is shared with the variant Jude. Both names carry the same meaning and reflect a common Hebrew root, emphasizing a theme of praise associated with this individual.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Judas as a brother of Jesus and infers that he was a son of Mary, establishing his direct kinship with the Messiah. Additionally, he is described as a brother to YHVH in an explicit relational sense, underscoring his familial connection to Christ.
scriptureSignificance: Judas’s significance lies in his identity as a biological brother of Jesus, born of Mary, which situates him within the Messianic lineage of the tribe of Judah. This connection underscores the fulfillment of Old Testament promises through the family line leading to the Messiah. His presence in the biblical narrative affirms the humanity and family context of Jesus Christ, the Lion of Judah.
